prompt: Stage 3-2 silver augment. You are level 6 with 39 gold at 48 HP on a 3-loss streak, losing about 8 HP a round. Your board is 2-star cheap units with one completed item on the carry, and you run two units of a trait whose next breakpoint is 4. Options: Sturdy Frontline (front two rows gain 150 HP and 12 armor), Compounding Interest (+1 interest per 10 gold, max +2) and Trait Heart (+1 to that trait). Which do you take?
explanation:
48 HP at 8 a loss is six losses in stage 3, but stage 4 losses cost 12 to 15, so you have about four losses of decisions left and you are losing every round. That puts you on the floor side of the line: the augment has to make the next fight better.

Sturdy Frontline does exactly that: 150 HP and 12 armor on three frontliners, this round and every round after. Compounding Interest is the trap for a player who loves econ: you are at 39 and losing, so the extra interest only exists once you sit above 50, and even then it is 1 or 2 gold a round for ten rounds, cashed at 4-5 when the HP is gone. Trait Heart takes the trait from 2 to 3 with the breakpoint at 4: it does nothing until you find and field another unit, and nothing is not power this round.

Silver augments are small, so the tie-break is always the one you can use before the timer ends.
principle: Below 50 HP and losing, take the silver augment that changes the next fight, not the one that pays in stage 5.
commonMistake: Taking the interest augment at 39 gold because it 'pays for itself', when it pays nothing until you are above 50 and still alive.
hint: Count how many losses you have left at the damage you are taking now, then ask which augment does anything before those losses run out.
